answer: No, the SIG never settled on a single answer. In the 'Rights model' thread (t0972, Feb-Mar 2017), Robert Sanderson raised the question of whether E30 Right is the abstract right/content of a right, or the instance of holding it, and Martin Doerr replied that there are really three distinct things -- the holding of the right, the content of the right, and the concept of the right -- and that whether holding can be merged with content 'is to be discussed.' The joint/partial ownership question (e.g., two people each owning 50% of an object, via P148_has_component) was raised in the same thread but Martin called it 'horribly complicated,' said the CRM was not built for such business-transaction modeling, and proposed splitting it off into a separate extension effort ('CRM social') rather than resolving it in CRM core. A related proposal for a new 'Right Holding' class with temporal properties (thread t0976) was submitted as an issue but not adopted. The follow-up thread 'End of Existence for Rights?' (t1019, Aug-Sep 2017) revisited the same abstract-concept-vs-instance dilemma; Martin's final reply there says a Right 'can be both' senses depending on context, suggests renaming E30 to something like 'Right Terms' and improving the scope note, but no e-vote or scope-note change is recorded closing the issue. The archive's own chronology for E30 marks both the 2017-02-28 and 2017-08-14 episodes as 'unresolved.'
